title: Guided Journey canonical route identity and deep-link resume

scope.subject: Give existing Guided Journeys stable route IDs and reloadable browser URLs while retaining the current Journey orchestration, canonical destination executor and interruption semantics

research_summary: Personal Universe already has a mature Guided Journey orchestration runtime: routes are derived from Places sections, every step calls the canonical destination executor, auto-advance waits for settled navigation, reduced-motion disables auto-advance, and manual navigation interrupts the journey. The remaining discovery gap is route identity/shareability. Reuse the existing browser History API and route derivation: centralize Featured/Projects/Research route construction in the navigation module, assign stable route IDs, store only journey=<id> and journeyStep=<index> in the existing URL, and reconstruct that route from canonical Places sections on reload. Destination deep-link execution must yield to Journey when a journey parameter is present so there is still one navigation owner. Stop/manual interruption clears only the Journey query parameters; destination/phase URLs remain authoritative.

sources.finding: The existing History API substrate can add/remove journey route parameters without introducing a client router or server state.
Pinned MIT YEIS TourPlayer validates route/tour orchestration concepts, while Personal Universe should retain its already-implemented lightweight Journey runtime rather than port narration/cue state.
Existing React effects can restore a URL-declared journey after content/marker state is available without creating a separate route runtime.
Existing hosted Playwright can verify Journey URL creation, reload restore, interruption cleanup and canonical destination continuity.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain the current Personal Universe Journey runtime and pinned-YEIS navigation model; only add route identity/share restoration.
Reuse browser History API and React effects instead of adding a router, server session or another journey state framework.
Keep existing settled-before-dwell and interruption semantics; centralize only the route derivation shared by Navigator and deep-link restore.
Reuse current Journey/URL browser acceptance and add deep-link resume assertions to the same release suite.

candidates.name: Existing Journey runtime plus History API route identity
candidates.source: Current UniverseApp Journey orchestration and canonical destination executor
candidates.license: project orchestration over pinned MIT YEIS
candidates.reason: Adds shareability without duplicating travel, settlement, interruption, destination identity or route execution.

candidates.name: History API journey/id step parameters
candidates.reason: Small shareable state belongs in the same URL already used for canonical destinations and phases.

candidates.name: Port or build a second TourPlayer state machine
candidates.reason: Would duplicate the already-working Journey executor and violate the one-navigation-authority constraint.

candidates.reason: A stable route ID and step index are sufficient for share/reload; server state adds unnecessary privacy and lifecycle surface.

coverage_matrix.capability: Journey route has one stable ID shared by discovery UI and reloadable URL
coverage_matrix.decision: Centralize route derivation and expose stable featured/projects/research IDs; URL stores route ID and bounded step only.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reload reconstructs the same route and current canonical destination without dual navigation ownership
coverage_matrix.decision: When journey is present, Journey restore owns initial destination execution and ordinary destination deep-link effect yields.

coverage_matrix.capability: Manual navigation/Stop interrupts Journey and removes only Journey URL state
coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse current interruption paths and clear journey/journeyStep parameters without changing destination/phase canonical URL.

decision.rationale: Add only stable route derivation and browser URL state around the existing Journey runtime. Navigation, settlement, camera, scale and destination identity remain owned by their current authorities.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Current Journey behavior is already productized; another runtime would create stale ownership and duplicate cancellation semantics.
URL route ID + step is sufficient for deterministic reload/share and avoids account/privacy/backend scope.

decision.fallback: If future journeys need narration or authored timing, extend route metadata around the same canonical route IDs; do not introduce a second destination executor or parallel navigation state machine.
